tasks.short: Attend regional denominational meetings, select programme materials to share, send them to small congregations, coach their leaders and plan interfaith activities with partners.

steps.what: Religious education director participates in regional denominational activities and meetings
Religious education director selects programme materials to share and removes local member details
Religious education director e-mails programme materials to small congregations one by one
Religious education director coaches leaders of new or small congregations by phone or visit
Religious education director plans interfaith activities with partners by e-mail

tasks.design: Programme materials the director has checked go into a shared library on the denomination's portal ({PARTNER_PORTAL}), so small congregations take what they need instead of receiving e-mails one by one. Interfaith activities are planned on a shared page with partners. Regional meetings and coaching leaders stay with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials went out by e-mail on request, and plans were spread over long threads.
tasks.enabler_now: Denominational portals host shared resource libraries; shared pages hold joint plans.
tasks.still_hard: Small congregations need encouragement more than documents.
tasks.human_edge: Building trust with a partner of another faith over coffee.

reach.learn: Whether the shared library gets used.

evidence.claim: Shared document libraries and planning pages can serve several organisations.
Church membership data may not be disclosed outside the religious body without consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the regional agenda to the interfaith plan; running the activities is outside.
Input contract: materials from the director's own programmes; portal library kept by the denomination's office; fallback is e-mail.
Small congregations download materials instead of reading e-mails; about the same time.
Meetings and coaching do not change.
research_questions: Do small congregations use more of the shared materials?

incremental.description: Religious education director tags shared materials by age and theme.

approvals.approved_version: The materials as selected and cleaned of member details by the director in s2.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few requests for materials; high: many small congregations asking for the same materials.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare talks and discussion evenings, speak and lead public discussions, write articles for publications, send them to the editor and answer the editor's questions.

steps.what: Religious education director prepares talks and discussion evenings
Religious education director interprets religious education activities to the public through speaking and leading discussions
Religious education director writes articles for local or national publications

loop.input: The director's outline, talk notes and the publication's word limit.
loop.output: A first draft of the article in the director's outline order.
loop.check: Code checks the word limit and that every quotation matches its source text; the director rewrites and approves the final text.
loop.stop: Approved by the director, or after two redrafts the director writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: An article needs prose; a template only gives headings.

steps.what: Religious education director sends the article to the editor
Religious education director answers the editor's questions and corrections

tasks.design: Talk notes and earlier articles are kept in one place in the document space ({DOCS}) for reuse. A bounded step turns the director's outline and notes into a first draft of an article; the director rewrites it and takes editorial responsibility before sending it to the editor. Speaking and leading discussions stay with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each article was written from a blank page.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft prose from an outline and notes.
tasks.still_hard: The voice and conviction of the text must be the director's own.
tasks.human_edge: Answering a hostile question in a public discussion with grace.
tasks.altitude: The director rewrites a first draft instead of starting blank.

reach.learn: Whether drafts arrive on time more often.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft an article from an outline and notes.
AI-generated text published to inform the public must be labelled unless a person reviews it and takes editorial responsibility.

assumptions: Boundary: from an invitation to the published article; the publication's editing is outside.
Input contract: outlines and notes by the director; word limits from the editor; fallback is writing from scratch.
Speaking and answering the editor do not change.
No member data go into the drafting step.
research_questions: How much of the draft survives the director's rewrite?

already_counted.description: Religious education director rewrites the drafted article.

incremental.description: Religious education director keeps talk notes filed for reuse.

approvals.approved_version: The article as rewritten and approved by the director in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few articles and mostly speaking; high: regular columns for publications.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set the conference theme and programme with co-organisers, invite speakers, take registrations, handle venue logistics, chair sessions and lead discussions, write the conference report and send it.

steps.what: Religious education director plans the conference theme and programme with co-organisers
Religious education director invites speakers by e-mail
Participants register by e-mail or phone
Religious education director handles registrations and venue logistics
Religious education director conducts conferences dealing with the interpretation of religious ideas, chairing sessions and discussions
Religious education director writes the conference report
Religious education director e-mails the report to participants

tasks.design: Speaker invitations start from a template with the programme details. Participants register and pay through an online form that builds the list and sends confirmations, and venue needs follow from the numbers. The report follows a fixed outline in the document space ({DOCS}) and goes to participants once the director has checked it. Planning the programme and chairing the conference stay with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Invitations, registrations and reports were handled by hand and by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Online registration forms and document templates are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Speakers on sensitive themes need personal persuasion.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a discussion on deep convictions respectful.

reach.learn: Whether shared registration lists cut double work.

evidence.claim: Online registration forms build participant lists and send confirmations.
Attendance at a religious conference can reveal religious belief, a special category of personal data.

assumptions: Boundary: from the conference idea to the report sent; conference finances are outside.
Input contract: programme agreed with co-organisers; venue options from the church administrator; fallback is e-mail and spreadsheets.
Participants register online instead of by e-mail; about the same time, priced as customer time.
Planning and chairing do not change.

incremental.description: Religious education director enters phone registrations in the form.

approvals.approved_version: The programme as agreed with co-organisers in s1.
The report as checked by the director in s6.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small conference with mostly phone registrations; high: a larger one with online registration.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The religious education director keeps speaking, coaching, chairing and building relationships; one-by-one e-mails, blank-page writing and registration lists shrink.
skills_to_grow: Rewriting drafted articles in their own voice
role.ambitious_version: A director who speaks and visits more and administers less.
